s: Edge-distributed content cache serving static assets from the nearest PoP to cut latency and absorb origin load.
w: Content is cached at hundreds of edge locations worldwide. First request fetches from origin (object_storage, api, or reverse_proxy) and caches; subsequent requests at that PoP are served from cache. Cache-Control headers and origin-push invalidation control freshness. TLS termination, Brotli compression, and image optimization happen at the edge. Surrogate-key purging enables selective invalidation.
use: Static asset delivery: JS bundles, CSS, images, fonts, video segments
API response caching for cacheable GET endpoints (product catalogs, search results)
DDoS absorption at the edge before traffic reaches origin
Edge compute (Workers/Lambda@Edge) for header manipulation and A/B tests
avoid: Frequently mutating personalized content (cache hit rate near zero = wasted hops)
Large binary uploads (CDN is for distribution not ingestion)
Strong consistency requirements without stale-while-revalidate tolerance

props.ttl_seconds: Default cache lifetime unless overridden by origin headers

size.rps_per_instance: Edge PoPs absorb millions rps; origin shielding reduces origin load ~90%

pat.d: CDN sits transparently; origin owns cache-control policy.

pits: Stale content after deploys - use surrogate-key purge and short TTLs during rollouts
Cache stampede on popular uncached origins - stale-while-revalidate + request coalescing
Overly broad cache invalidation purging everything - surgical surrogate-key discipline
tips: Cache hit ratio is the headline metric: >90% is healthy; investigate misses
Origin shield / mid-tier caching reduces cost and origin load dramatically
